items.headline: Two unanimous MVPs — Alvarez and Crow-Armstrong sweep the vote
items.body: Awards week ended with a bang: Houston's Yordan Alvarez (AL) and the Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong (NL) were both named MVP unanimously — every single first-place vote. Alvarez led the majors in average, on-base and slugging; PCA paired 45 homers with Gold Glove center-field defense. Two unanimous winners in one year is a rarity.
items.say: Both MVPs were unanimous this year — Yordan Alvarez and the Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong. You almost never see that. You keep up with baseball at all?

items.headline: It's finally here — Gen.G vs Bilibili Gaming for the Worlds crown Saturday
items.body: The League of Legends World Championship ends Saturday at Brooklyn's Barclays Center: Gen.G — chasing a first-ever title after years of semifinal heartbreak — meet China's Bilibili Gaming in a best-of-five. K/DA and True Damage headline the opening ceremony, so even the pre-show is a spectacle.
items.say: The League of Legends world final is Saturday in Brooklyn — Gen.G finally has their shot at the title. You ever dip into any esports?

items.headline: Back to Panem — 'Sunrise on the Reaping' tells young Haymitch's story
items.body: The next Hunger Games film, 'Sunrise on the Reaping,' hits theaters November 20 — the 50th Games (the Second Quarter Quell) with a young Haymitch Abernathy at its center. Joseph Zada stars alongside Elle Fanning, Ralph Fiennes and Jesse Plemons, and the soundtrack album drops today.
items.say: There's a new Hunger Games coming — it's young Haymitch's origin story. The teaser apparently broke view records. You into those movies?

links.text: Sunrise on the Reaping — official trailer (Lionsgate)

items.headline: Netflix dramatizes the FTX implosion — 'The Altruists' lands Nov 19
items.body: Julia Garner (as Caroline Ellison) and Anthony Boyle (as Sam Bankman-Fried) star in Netflix's eight-episode limited series on the dizzying rise and spectacular collapse of crypto exchange FTX. All episodes drop at once on November 19.
items.say: Netflix made a show about the whole FTX crypto blowup — Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle. That saga was bonkers. You remember when all that went down?

items.headline: Tennis's season finale starts Sunday — Alcaraz headlines Turin, no Sinner
items.body: The eight best men wrap up the year at the Nitto ATP Finals in Turin, beginning Sunday. World No. 1 Carlos Alcaraz is the clear favorite with defending champ Jannik Sinner sidelined by a season-ending knee injury, and young countryman Rafael Jodar grabbing the final spot as the surprise debutant.
items.say: The ATP Finals start Sunday — Alcaraz is the man to beat now that Sinner's hurt. You catch any tennis?

links.text: The eight-man field is set (ATP Tour)

items.headline: J.J. Abrams is back — 'The Great Beyond' opens today
items.body: J.J. Abrams' first original film since 2011 hits theaters today: a reality-bending sci-fi mystery starring Glen Powell and Jenna Ortega, with Samuel L. Jackson in the cast. Big swing, big names — very much a see-it-on-the-biggest-screen kind of movie.
items.say: J.J. Abrams has a new sci-fi movie out today with Glen Powell and Jenna Ortega — his first original in ages. You a fan of his stuff?

items.headline: Becky Hill goes all-in on the dancefloor with 'REBECCA'
items.body: The British hitmaker — one of the UK's biggest dance-pop voices — is out with 'REBECCA,' a glossy, made-for-the-dancefloor record led by singles like 'what do i have to do?'. Easy, upbeat weekend listening.
items.say: Becky Hill's got a new album — proper feel-good dance-pop. Great Friday-night stuff. You into any of that?

links.text: Becky Hill — what do i have to do? (Official Video)

items.headline: Jake Bugg returns with 'Alamo,' out today
items.body: The Nottingham singer-songwriter — of 'Lightning Bolt' and 'Two Fingers' fame — drops his new album 'Alamo' today, led by the breezy single 'Never Can Tell.' Still that unmistakable reedy voice and knack for a hook.
items.say: New Jake Bugg album out today — if you ever liked that scrappy British songwriter sound, it's right up your alley. You know him?
